note: Authored understanding of each project, written from the per-file content records and measured wiring on 2026-11-15. `what` = what it is and how it works; `use` = what the founder uses it for. Statements about state quote dated repository documents or measured static wiring; they are not runtime or outcome proof. Edit by hand; `npm run repo:index` renders them.

wessam-singularity.what: The top of the hierarchy: a founder-level research program asking whether the machinery that produces your future selves and options can undergo a real regime change. It is defined as falsifiable, with a continuity module that packs your cognitive state into portable recovery capsules.
wessam-singularity.use: Orienting everything beneath it, and carrying founder continuity across providers. It is a target, never a claimed result.

sovereign-continuum.what: UberBond's terminal identity: you supply will, the system supplies intelligence, reality supplies feedback. The code here is the guard layer around that relation: a living model of you that refuses to freeze your identity, privacy views over your context, typed ignorance and bias attacks on conclusions, and an intent compiler that traces a choice through permissions to observed consequences.
sovereign-continuum.use: Keeping any amount of intelligence from turning into authority over what you want; the constitution every session reads first.

personal-civilization.what: The life-system layer. A private life record with provable export and deletion, a provenance-carrying life knowledge graph, an options scorer that compares life choices per dimension without collapsing them into one number, a futures inventory showing which branches a decision opens or closes, and a human capability graph that searches for your binding bottleneck.
personal-civilization.use: Seeing your life options, capabilities and consequences clearly while you remain the chooser. About half its modules are not yet wired to any entry point.

forecast-engine.what: The decision-science organ: forecast methods that compete on hindcast accuracy, an ensemble that discounts forecasters sharing the same evidence, a sealed calibration ledger that scores forecasts against outcomes and separates forecast accuracy from decision quality, and a value-of-information governor that says when to stop researching.
forecast-engine.use: Getting option sets with honest outcome ranges before a material decision, and learning over time which methods deserve trust.

ubermind.what: The cognition doctrine and its economics. Doctrine: constitutions V4 to V10, the Omega46-52 lens cards, the founder 52 concepts and the grand library. Code: cost models for model mixes and agent meshes, a topology chooser that sizes cognition to consequence and reversibility, and exact source-work accounting.
ubermind.use: Telling every assistant how to think and report (the receipts), and deciding how much model spend a task deserves. Mostly doctrine; most of its modules are not wired.

phoenix.what: Context survival. A context journal with projections, task bindings and schema versioning, so each task gets only its bound slice of context and a brain state can be carried as a capsule with integrity and freshness. Around it: the PHOENIX protocol, an MCP connector with eight tools, 15 deterministic zero-effect handlers and capability waves 3 to 10.
phoenix.use: Resuming in a new chat without retelling the project. The October 24 checkpoint records MCP tests passing and ChatGPT registration unverified.

brain-memory.what: The repository's own memory and self-model: a cognitive graph of organs with typed edges, an event bus and append-only journal over it, a lifetime memory index across episodic, semantic, economic and evidence layers, plus Total Brain and Master Memory as the anti-forgetting canon of programs and lineage.
brain-memory.use: Reconstructing the whole organism before narrowing to a task; the brain packet you run at startup comes from here.

handoffs-checkpoints.what: The dated trail of where work stopped: the current handoff and system state, per-session handoffs, crash-safe checkpoints and the entry-point files assistants read first. Documents only, no source modules.
handoffs-checkpoints.use: Picking up exactly where a previous session left off, and seeing what was true on a given date.

apotheosis-orchestration.what: Your orchestration specification made executable: packets P00 to P49, a runtime that selects context policy, allocates scarce strong-model reasoning, routes work down to cheaper models and hands off continuity, and a graph validator that tournaments orchestration candidates.
apotheosis-orchestration.use: Running large multi-agent builds in dependency order. Gate 4, real closed-loop evidence, is recorded as externally blocked.

historical-lineage.what: The record of earlier named programs: Everest, SUMMIT 100, BLACK SKY, Reality Activation, Ragnarok, Night War, with their closure receipts and the register of external gates still open.
historical-lineage.use: Not forgetting what older programs donated, and seeing honest closure verdicts such as NIGHT-10 meeting 9 of 11 obligations.

work-astra-sol.what: The prompts, bootstraps and packet queues that drive GPT Work, Astra and Sol sessions and Claude mega-missions, including the progress baseline and the launch package that splits readiness into purchase, send, collection and delivery.
work-astra-sol.use: Starting a working session for another assistant with the right mission and reporting format.

genesis.what: The invention engine. A mechanism compiler with stable statement identity, idea bursts drawn from the million-branch genome, an ontology and scientist layer, an escalation tribunal that decides implement, escalate or wait for reality, and an evidence ledger showing which of the 275 registry ideas have code behind them.
genesis.use: Generating and testing new mechanisms and ideas nobody asked for, cheaply and without external effects. Reachable from CLI commands, not from the server.

moonshot-890.what: Your 890 original ideas as an immutable, hash-verified corpus in ten shards, plus what is compiled from it: a realization state machine, a technology tree, a triage of which moonshots can be realized internally, a substrate mesh and a portfolio ranking of shared ancestor capabilities.
moonshot-890.use: Retrieving any original idea exactly, and choosing which shared building blocks to construct first. Source-complete does not mean realized.

gamechanger.what: Always-on world sensing: a mesh over sixteen domains that canonicalizes, dedupes and scores public signals, paces polling within provider rate limits, and turns discoveries into frontier learning inputs and combinable idea packets.
gamechanger.use: Noticing early when the outside world changes what is possible for you or the system.

million-wormhole.what: Combinatorial ideation at scale: an index that encodes a million cross-organ candidates, operators that generate them, shard tournaments, and a spec of 20 domains by 50 operators extending the 275-idea registry.
million-wormhole.use: Searching far, low-similarity combinations of existing organs for ideas ordinary brainstorming would miss.

temporal-foundry.what: Reasoning about time order: analyses of future capability states, a timeline topology engine that looks for shortcuts across planned timelines, and an epoch-branching evaluator with ancestor ablation over the 890 technology tree.
temporal-foundry.use: Asking which future capability can be pulled forward and which prerequisite actually matters. Source-level only; none of its modules are wired.

neural-exocortex.what: A large external capability memory: a neural capability corpus with priors and merge rules, harvest storage outside working memory, a repository atlas plan, and the Connectome rule that every new feature must join the organ graph through typed edges.
neural-exocortex.use: Holding far more capability knowledge than fits in context and finding missing links between modules.

sandwich-method.what: A work-decomposition method: pair exact current reality with a stronger descendant design, then fold the gap into bounded missions and canonical leaves, with governors for self-continuing tasks and evidence bound to each plan.
sandwich-method.use: Turning a big ambition into small verifiable steps that agents can execute. Not wired to any entry point.

frontier.what: The multi-model reasoning runtime: plans cognition across reasoning tiers with a context spine, proves a frontier model is actually callable before use, admits models only with sealed benchmark evidence, and harvests frontier AI mechanisms from public sources.
frontier.use: Getting frontier-grade answers by composing models instead of trusting one, and absorbing new techniques as they appear.

apex.what: The experiment that tests the cost-compression claim: sealed architecture trials with committed digests and NULLSTAR holdouts, identity-blind packets, fresh campaigns under the zero-loss quality rule, and a handoff for an external custodian to supply unseen tasks.
apex.use: Finding out, falsifiably, whether a cheaper architecture really matches the strongest model.

nullstar.what: A self-evaluation program: seeded task generators across planning, science, causality, tool use, research, invention and forecasting, a harness that strips ground truth before solving, sealed holdouts, out-of-pattern probes, and pre-registered improvement declarations across generations G1 to G8.
nullstar.use: Measuring whether the system genuinely improves between generations rather than memorizing its tests. Every module is reachable from a command.

omega-lab.what: A private evidence lab of controlled mathematical and causal canaries (cube-free, power-free, multiplicity-depth, causal compilers), with independent replications and a standard that reserves top marks for adversarial hidden-holdout results.
omega-lab.use: Held-out probes of reasoning capability. It is self-contained research: 34 of 35 modules are not connected to anything else.

c21-asi-evidence.what: The honesty gate on superintelligence claims: canonical evidence dimensions and external benchmark surfaces, an evaluator that rejects cosmetic aliases, and a tribunal that refuses literal ASI claims without system-level evidence.
c21-asi-evidence.use: Stating the ASI status truthfully. The September 11 inventory records zero authenticated system-level receipts.

inevitability-v9.what: A lossless, hash-locked carrier for the 146 MB Inevitability Engine V9 text, stored as a compressed V7 seed plus the deterministic generator for V8 and V9.
inevitability-v9.use: Rebuilding that exact source file on demand without keeping a 146 MB blob in git.

infinite-opus.what: The intelligence-per-dollar program. A durable runtime with monthly budgets and Decision Franchises required before any paid call, a live model price market, a zero-loss quality invariant that forbids routing below the strongest baseline, and an OpenAI-compatible gateway serving your TypingMind iPad cockpit.
infinite-opus.use: Running strong-model-quality work on roughly a 30 dollar monthly budget. The most wired cognition project; realized savings remain unmeasured.

crown.what: The strongest-model seat and its rules: exact model revision pinning, admission receipts, sealed checkpoints, safe resume of interrupted paid generations, a proof interpreter that checks outputs close their obligations, and a succession process with quarantine and hidden battery.
crown.use: Guaranteeing the final judge is the real strongest model and that promotions to that seat are earned. Almost fully wired into the server.

jev-uberlit.what: Jev is the cheap fast semantic judge; UberLit is the host service it runs on. Jev coalesces same-scope questions into one paid call, keeps a calibration vault, reuses already-billed answers, and a noetic autocompiler turns verified cognition into cheaper reflexes.
jev-uberlit.use: Handling routine judgements cheaply so only unresolved questions reach the Crown.

model-routing.what: The model market: one factory creating executors for OpenAI, Anthropic, Claude Code sandbox and Vercel gateway, a governed OpenRouter adapter, a router that subtracts known per-task weaknesses, failover bound to approved workers, and receipts of which provider actually ran.
model-routing.use: Picking the right model for each task and continuing through another when one hits a limit, with the real model identity recorded.

semantic-closure.what: The exactness kernel: canonical semantic hashing, a finite opcode executor, a closure checker with circuit certificates, and an execution-leaf graph of remaining work with resumable continuations and tamper-evident digests.
semantic-closure.use: Proving a task is actually closed before authority or money is spent on it, and resuming bounded leaves across sessions.

cognition-ledger.what: The meter on every model call: a reserve, dispatch, settle, release ledger recording actual cost and request fingerprints, hard all-in dollar caps with a Crown reserve, an inventory of every route that can spend, and a transport guard that refuses calls outside the economic perimeter.
cognition-ledger.use: Making it impossible to overspend on cognition by accident.

reasoning-lab.what: Evaluation machinery for compound intelligence: a parent tribunal with anti-gaming laws, cross-domain transfer measurement, novelty checks on challenges, and frozen independent holdouts that judge fresh-context retention.
reasoning-lab.use: Testing whether a learned mechanism transfers and persists, without promoting it on its own say-so.

agent-mesh.what: The autonomous worker system: an autonomy loop with attenuation-only delegation and compute ceilings, durable run snapshots, cycle receipts that expose crashed cycles, a code-change contract that protects verification paths, and sandbox verification of agent edits.
agent-mesh.use: Letting agents do bounded work while you are away, with every cycle accounted for.

relay.what: The transport between assistants: a cloud relay storing task packets as leased jobs, a GitHub Issues relay with claim and heartbeat comments, canonical multi-worker task and dispute packets, and a pinned Vercel preview deployment.
relay.use: Passing tasks between ChatGPT, Claude Code and cloud workers with leases and receipts.

uber-socket.what: A live bridge between chat apps: a runtime wiring a conversation adapter, project mesh, shared content fabric and cognitive backplane, with persisted state, plus a Chrome extension pairing two ChatGPT tabs over an encrypted channel.
uber-socket.use: Making separate chat sessions share context in real time. All nine modules are wired into the server.

ai-employees.what: AI workers as bounded employees: role contracts that define what each role may do and refuse undeclared role claims, and the Avengers arsenal that registers model and tool profiles, probes readiness and composes squads by evidence.
ai-employees.use: Assigning the right squad to a mission and keeping generic work from posing as privileged.

night.what: The overnight lanes: Night Shift, Nightfall and Ragnarok-era parallel lanes with coordination rules and zero default external effects, synthetic journey diagnostics, and owner-reviewable upgrade manifests.
night.use: Running coordinated overnight builds and reading in the morning exactly what was produced. Mostly historical now.

self-maintainer.what: Governed self-upgrade: a continuation gate, GitHub OIDC verification before any authority, authority limited to branch and pull request, enforced separation of proposer, evaluator, approver and deployer, and a Mutation War inventory of 58 guard mutations that tests must kill.
self-maintainer.use: Letting the system propose and test its own improvements without being able to weaken its own checks.

assistant-integrations.what: How each assistant plugs in: Claude Code project memory and settings, the project MCP server exposing state and relay tools, a ChatGPT project importer, and pointers for Gemini, Cursor and Codex.
assistant-integrations.use: Getting any assistant correctly oriented in this repository from its first message.

capability-genome.what: The governed supplier market for capabilities: a typed schema, discovery from registered sources, normalization of public skill bodies, dedupe, license and instruction-scan admission, minimum-bundle retrieval and capability-by-model routing.
capability-genome.use: Finding and safely adopting an outside capability when a real gap appears. Zero capabilities are approved or active so far.

wallbreaker.what: The stuck-mission solver: compile the wall, generate materially different strategy families, score them under hard constraints, classify failures and derive countermoves, with a failure-to-patch reflex.
wallbreaker.use: Breaking a repeated failure without retrying the same thing. It plans only and carries no authority.

skills-plugins.what: Project skills and their governance: the UberSkills atom framework and its wrappers, the skills under `.claude/skills`, plugins, the Task Observer log, and the canon for vetting external skills and orchestration donors.
skills-plugins.use: Reusable procedures assistants can invoke, and the rule for admitting new ones.

omnia.what: The admission kernel between intelligence and consequence: creates and verifies action intents, evidence, approvals and execution receipts, answers allow, review or deny, and provides a provider-neutral effect adapter contract and Cedar policy. Carries the OMNIA lineage X10 to V9 and the V7 mission graph.
omnia.use: The final gate on any consequential action. About a third of its 52 modules are wired.

authority-evidence.what: The shared truth plumbing nearly everything imports: one vocabulary for external-effect ledgers, a content-addressed proof graph, consent receipts suitable for CASL and GDPR, provider payload redaction, and a router that stops internal work from declaring completion when the missing proof is external.
authority-evidence.use: Making every claim traceable and every side effect counted. It is the most depended-on project in the repository.

readiness-audits.what: The self-honesty tools: a capability inventory with statuses, a no-drop coverage compiler with one row per canon concept, a check that coverage cannot overclaim, proof that current-truth artifacts regenerate at head, and the doctor scripts.
readiness-audits.use: Knowing what is actually implemented, reachable and regenerable, as opposed to documented.

uberwarm.what: Mailbox warmup you control: owner-approved seed probes with exact-form validation, one-shot send capabilities bound to a single approved send, a fail-closed check that adverse events are suppressed before sending, and a reputation lab setting conservative ramp caps.
uberwarm.use: Building sender reputation before any cold email, with evidence instead of trust in a vendor's 'warmed' label. Most modules are donor or protected paths not yet wired.

winnr.what: The Winnr provider integration: an API client under a zero-paid route policy, token scope inspection, credential import, and a post-purchase bootstrap that registers bought domains and mailboxes into the sending fleet.
winnr.use: Buying and onboarding pre-warmed mailboxes for first cash. The October 8 evidence shows the 69 dollar purchase awaiting your spend confirmation.

ubermail-uberdoso.what: An owned mail stack: UberDoso topology over your roots and the 28-domain fleet with sender selection and cooldown, a Postal-based mail cell, safe-failure SMTP submission, and UberMail, an inbox API for agents.
ubermail-uberdoso.use: Sending and receiving mail on infrastructure you own instead of renting each mailbox.

inboxes-placement.what: Inbox supply and quality: an IMAP reader, adapters for mailbox vendors with approval-gated writes, placement probes that fail closed on identity mismatch, and attention permits gating sender access to recipients.
inboxes-placement.use: Reading replies and knowing whether mail lands in the inbox or spam.

dns-domains.what: The domain and DNS layer: authoritative records of your owned domains, a plan separating product, outbound, reply and tracking hosts, append-only registries of every sending domain and mailbox, and an encrypted SMTP fleet with approval digests.
dns-domains.use: Knowing the exact state of every sending domain and mailbox before trusting it with a send.

outreach.what: The outreach core: route policy and approval governance, canonical send eligibility with time zones, volume windows and suppression, a launch gate requiring adverse provider events reconciled first, Gmail transport, and invitation codes that turn an offline first touch into permissioned email.
outreach.use: Deciding whether a specific contact may be messaged, and sending only through that gate. The most server-wired commercial project.

prospecting-leadgen.what: Finding and qualifying who to contact: lead signal stacking and scoring, a suppression and prior-contact history compiler, evidence-class clamping that prevents laundering weak evidence, contact verification, and zero-cost company registry adapters.
prospecting-leadgen.use: A ranked list of real prospects with verified facts and no one you have already contacted or suppressed.

uberreach-uberoutbound.what: Outbound strategy as policy: an evidence-weighted message genome, a per-recipient legal eligibility decision naming the rule, channel-neutral reach planning, and the postal sender identity required for compliant sends.
uberreach-uberoutbound.use: Designing what to say and confirming you are legally allowed to say it to that person.

reply-closing.what: What happens after someone answers: four offer lanes with fit scoring, the prework artifact promised in the first touch, a reply classifier that halts automation on any material human reply and routes it to you, and the async-first funnel to payment.
reply-closing.use: Closing without meetings by default, with every real human reply handled by you personally.

distribution-os.what: Distribution as an allocation problem: a channel registry that ranks only channels backed by cleared-payment outcomes, a portfolio compiler with a cap of half per channel, a router to non-email first touch when cold email is ineligible, and an agent-commerce surface.
distribution-os.use: Deciding where the next unit of distribution effort should go.

revenue-payments.what: Payment truth: reconciliation of cleared payments, refunds and renewals, Lemon Squeezy and PayPal event classification with signature checks, and fail-closed facades that refuse replayed or incomplete provider evidence.
revenue-payments.use: Knowing what money has actually cleared, never counting a link or an invoice as revenue.

revenue-constellation.what: The commercial cockpit: a service binding snapshot, radar and X-ray to the store, honest funnel statistics with intervals and the earliest broken stage, the Money Queue ranking who gets the next governed first touch, G-SPOT one-button orchestration, and a signed owner session.
revenue-constellation.use: Seeing the whole funnel on your iPad and advancing it with one governed action. Fully wired; the October 5 receipt lists a legal hold as the remaining blocker.

first-cash.what: The path to the first cleared payment: a nineteen-question readiness packet where permission to contact is a pure function of six gates, a canary capped by qualified conversations, and a seven-day first-payment packet.
first-cash.use: Answering whether you are ready for a first customer, with evidence for each gate.

offers-fulfilment.what: What is sold and how it is delivered: offer packets with deliverables, exclusions and timeline, the lead-path sprint with payment validated before fulfilment, a pay-per-verified-finding product, and a state machine from delivery through acceptance to renewal.
offers-fulfilment.use: Defining the offer and tracking a paid order to accepted delivery.

economic-engines.what: Economic reasoning tools: founder outcome missions, a reliability engine that ranks actions by how much they raise the chance of non-zero money, candidate dispositions from probe to scale, a wealth-mechanism grammar with prohibited patterns, and a check for routes sharing one failure point.
economic-engines.use: Choosing which money path to work on next and avoiding false redundancy.

inquiry-audit-product.what: The original product: a website lead-path audit. A robots-respecting crawler and read-only fetcher, deterministic audit rules, an engine that finds sites contradicting themselves on contact channels, and the intake-to-paid-report flow.
inquiry-audit-product.use: Producing verified problem evidence for a prospect; it is both a sellable audit and the proof used in first touches.

client-engagements.what: Records about specific counterparties: Powerhouse proof rechecks and scope, a drafted Contra project and collection readiness, and a Halfteck supplier packet.
client-engagements.use: The exact state of each real prospect or supplier conversation. The Contra project is a draft, not created or sent.

lite-cash-engine.what: A standalone free-tier variant of the audit product: static site, serverless API, an Actions-based audit worker and Postgres. Kept separate from the main application.
lite-cash-engine.use: A cheap deployable version of the audit funnel. Do not modify without a separately justified mission.

quant-lab.what: Research-only market analysis: checksum-verified public data, a backtester with no lookahead, explicit costs and deflated Sharpe, pre-registered strategy families, and a hash-chained paper ledger that cannot place orders.
quant-lab.use: Killing false trading edges honestly. No live trading capability or authority; not wired to anything.

prometheus.what: The market-sensing spine: a source-neutral signal schema with evidence classes, ingestion, conversion of signals into Business Genome candidates, and evidence-gated commercial learning that never infers revenue.
prometheus.use: Turning world observations into candidate opportunities. All ten modules are wired into the server.

opportunity-factory.what: Opportunity selection: a Business Genome compiler and tournament that caps confidence by evidence class, a catalog of 438 deduplicated opportunities with three buyer-signal finalists, mechanism recombination with red-teaming, and Event Horizon validation.
opportunity-factory.use: Choosing the single commercial experiment worth running now, from a wide evidence-labelled field.

command-center.what: Your control surface: the iPad Command Center and admin pages, an autonomy status report, client rules that keep stale data from looking live, a founder report on what can make money first, and an allocator for your scarce attention.
command-center.use: Watching and steering the system from one screen with a short, exact owner-action queue.

kilimanjaro.what: Founder-absence readiness: classifies every blocker to unattended operation and whether code can remove it, scores absence from durable history, and tracks whether an escalation actually reached your device.
kilimanjaro.use: Knowing honestly how close the system is to running while you are away. It records that no escalation transport reaching a human device ships yet.

green-lane.what: The lawful-route finder: a freshness-checked registry of jurisdiction and provider rules, a router through legal form, recipient type, consent and cost to the best permitted route, and a classifier of invited versus cold contact from dated evidence.
green-lane.use: Finding the lowest-friction contact route that is actually permitted for each prospect, or stopping.

sovereign-selfhost.what: Running on your own hardware: release handoff to offline packs, compute allocation by ownership and rights, a capacity frontier of owned versus rented compute, an institutional engineering harness, and the Docker images and install scripts under `ops/sovereign`.
sovereign-selfhost.use: Independence from any single cloud or model provider. Largely tests and plans; no module is server-wired.

ubercel-cloud.what: An owned deployment plane: provider-neutral deploy and failover planning, a control plane treating cloud suppliers as replaceable cells, Contabo cell preflight, and a static deployment store with rollback.
ubercel-cloud.use: Deploying and moving services across providers without lock-in. Plans grant no authority; mostly unwired.

uberos.what: A sovereign operating-system program: generation 0 is a minimal Buildroot Linux with UberBond authority, package provenance and kernel-adapter contracts. Linux is treated as the first replaceable kernel.
uberos.use: A long-horizon substrate under your control. It does not claim to have replaced Linux or booted on your hardware.

uberwatt.what: Energy accounting for compute: meter intervals, verified savings and energy-equivalent local inference, with an observation-only protocol to build a household baseline first.
uberwatt.use: Eventually budgeting local compute against real energy. One module, observation stage.

data-stores.what: Persistence: JSON and Postgres stores implementing every collection with reservation transactions, a durable job queue with leases, full-history audit paging, migrations and embedded Postgres test fixtures.
data-stores.use: Where all durable state lives; nearly every runtime project writes through it.

platform-deploy.what: How it is hosted: Vercel, Render, Railway, Docker and Cloudflare configuration, CI workflows, systemd units and install scripts, plus receipts proving restart recovery and that a release booted on an independent host.
platform-deploy.use: Deploying, restarting and proving the service can move hosts.

core-platform.what: The shared base: server and worker entry points, central config with startup validation, one secret-pattern scanner, encryption, strict input parsing, and the test runner.
core-platform.use: The foundation every other project stands on.

neu205.what: A separate study-tool engineering continuation with a public, source-only recovery document. Private course material, answer keys and build secrets are deliberately not in the repository.
neu205.use: Resuming that side project in Claude Code without exposing private assets.
